$comment: Tests that fail BY DESIGN because strape changes upstream behaviour. Any deviation from this exact set fails CI: a new failure is a regression, and an expected failure that starts passing means upstream changed the test and this entry needs re-examining. Never add an entry without a reason.

test/config.test.ts > detectInstallMetho.rootCause: The test reaches getSelfUpdateCommandForMethod, whose pnpm branch SPAWNS a real package manager: packages/coding-agent/src/config.ts:126 calls readCommandOutput("pnpm", ["root", "-g"]). Its runtime therefore depends on the host toolchain, not on anything strape changed.
test/config.test.ts > detectInstallMetho.observed: On the recording machine pnpm is a Volta shim (~/.volta/bin/pnpm) and ./test.sh isolates HOME (test.sh:43), so Volta finds no tool image under the fake HOME and tries to provision one over the network — the test exceeds its 30s timeout. Reproduced 3/3 in the full suite, including on an otherwise idle machine, while passing 15/15 across three isolated runs of config.test.ts and passing on a GitHub runner.
test/config.test.ts > detectInstallMetho.whyExcluded: Both outcomes are correct for their host. Asserting either one guarantees a permanently red gate on the other side, and a gate that is always red somewhere is one people stop reading. It is excluded in both directions and reported instead.

test/openai-completions-tool-choice.test.rootCause: Decided by live third-party data, not by strape or by the adopted upstream tag. The test asserts compat.maxTokensField === "max_tokens" for opencode/opencode-go models. Upstream .gitignore:11 excludes packages/ai/src/providers/data/, so upstream generates the model catalog from models.dev at every build; hunk 6 vendors it so strape can build offline. models.dev changed those models API shape after v0.84.1 was tagged, so the assertion no longer holds — for upstream too, not just for strape.
test/openai-completions-tool-choice.test.observed: Fails identically on every host and in CI as of 2026-08-09. The same drift produces a tsgo error at openai-completions-tool-choice.test.ts:1410. Full analysis in review-v0.84.1.md.
test/openai-completions-tool-choice.test.whyExcluded: It will start passing again the moment models.dev or upstream realigns, with no strape change. Asserting either outcome makes the gate wrong on one side of that event. Excluded in both directions and reported instead. Re-check at the next sync: if it has realigned, delete this entry.

test/first-time-setup.test.ts > shouldRu.reason: Asserts shouldRunFirstTimeSetup() is true with experimental features on, the default agent dir and no settings.json (test:37). It returns false at the first guard: isOfficialDistribution({PACKAGE_NAME, APP_NAME, CONFIG_DIR_NAME}) is false for any fork (cli/startup-ui.ts:36-42, 115-124), and hunk 1 sets piConfig.name/configDir to strape/.strape. Documented as a deliberate side effect in strape/docs/HUNKS.md hunk 1: the first-run wizard is disabled and strape/scripts/claude-compat.mjs seeds settings instead. The three sibling tests asserting false all pass, which is what confirms the guard rather than the wiring is responsible.

test/package-command-paths.test.ts > pac.reason: Asserts the stubbed fetch is called exactly once during `update --self` (test:487). Hunk 10 returns shouldRun:false at package-manager-cli.ts:492-505 BEFORE getLatestPiRelease, so pi.dev is never contacted — observed 'expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times'. That the version check never happens is the hunk, not a side effect of it.

The test reads join(projectDir, ".pi", "settings.json") directly (test:351-352); hunk 1 sets piConfig.configDir to .strape, so `install -l` writes .strape/settings.json and the test's own readFileSync throws. Observed as ENOENT on .../project/.pi/settings.json at test:352 — a missing file in the pre-rebrand location, NOT a missing binary or a failed install: the settings were written one directory over. Intended rebrand.

Intended rebrand.

Writes .pi/settings.json so the project counts as trust-requiring (test:334), then asserts the install is refused with "Project is not trusted. Use --approve to modify local package config." and exitCode 1. The trust boundary is intact; the test's marker file is in the pre-rebrand location. Note the FIRST-load path here is upstream's; the reload half of that boundary is hunk 11 and is pinned by trust-regression-test.mjs.
